newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police hold Reuters cameraman in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police hold Reuters cameraman in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli police detained a Reuters television cameraman in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday when he tried to film the arrest of a Palestinian journalist at an Israeli military checkpoint.
The cameraman, Mazen Dana, was taken away for questioning at a police post, an Israeli police spokesman said.
Film of the incident by another cameraman present showed an Israeli soldier approach Dana and attempt to prevent him from recording the arrest of the local woman journalist by two Israeli policemen.
It showed Dana surrounded and jostled by five soldiers, one of whom used a stranglehold, following an exchange of words. Dana was driven away in a police vehicle.
An army spokesman said the incident was a police matter.
The police spokesman, Ofer Sivan, said Dana had been detained because soldiers said he had "disturbed" their work.
"He is now in investigation. When we have finished our investigation I expect he will be released," Sivan said.

Israel has imposed a security clampdown on parts of the West Bank where it still has forces in a hunt for Islamists militants following an attack on a Jerusalem market by two suicide bombers on Wednesday which killed 15 people.

Israel handed over about 80 percent of Hebron -- home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers -- to the PLO under peace deals last January but keeps soldiers in the rest of the town to protect Jewish enclaves.

Hebron was the scene of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops after a right-wing Jewish woman pasted posters on storefronts in the town last month depicting the Moslem prophet Mohammad as a pig.
The violence subsided when Palestinian police intervened two weeks ago but flares up occasionally.
